audit_findings.title: FY2025 OE may carry a stale interest burden for the 2026 capital structure
audit_findings.magnitude: $500.0 million notes repaid; June 2026 debt was $4,848.955 million versus $4,364.678 million at December 2025; first-half 2026 interest before extinguishment loss was $88.549 million versus $91.627 million in first-half 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest remains in equity-level OE, so any difference between FY2025 interest and the sustainable 2026 burden changes anchor OE and every projected year.
audit_findings.explanation: The capital structure has changed, but a valuation error is not yet demonstrated. The notes were repaid using revolver borrowings and cash, June debt was higher than year-end debt, and the related U.S. interest-rate swaps expired; however, reported first-half interest was $3.078 million lower year over year. Seasonality and the mix and rates of replacement borrowing prevent the record from establishing either direction or materiality for normalized annual interest.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each debt instrument, revolver balance, hedge maturity and effective rate through 2026; calculate normalized annual after-tax interest and rerun OE if it differs from the FY2025 burden.

audit_findings.title: Recurring rationalization costs may have been stripped from anchor OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $60.509 million FY2025 charge, equal to 16.8% of $359.9 million anchor OE; $26.1 million FY2025 cash payments; $37.1 million remaining cash expenditures at year-end; $27.206 million additional charges in first-half 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding recurring rationalization charges back to earnings raises anchor OE; omitting associated recurring cash expenditures also raises projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: While rationalization costs are incurred on a regular basis, management views these costs more as an investment to generate savings rather than period costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied record does not demonstrate that the valuation actually added back the charge because the OE adjustment ledger is absent. If it did, the issue is reasonably capable of changing the valuation: rationalization is explicitly regular, continued into 2026, and the FY2025 charge alone was 16.8% of anchor OE. Noncash asset write-downs may warrant different treatment, but that does not justify removing recurring severance, exit or replacement expenditures.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 OE ledger by charge component, retain recurring cash severance and plant-exit costs, separately evaluate the $18.550 million noncash write-down, and rerun all scenarios with the corrected anchor and future rationalization cash needs.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $351.527 million, or $3.28 per diluted share; removing all of it would reduce computed bear value from $43.21 to $39.93 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all June 2026 cash to equity value even though cash needed for seasonal working capital is an operating asset and should not be added separately.
audit_findings.evidence: Our peak seasonal working capital borrowings have historically averaged approximately $600 million and were generally funded with revolving loans under our Credit Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: It is demonstrated that the bridge adds the entire cash balance, but it is unresolved how much is excess. At the same date Silgan had $1,075.902 million of revolver borrowings and had used $993.850 million of operating cash during the first half for the seasonal working-capital build. The full $351.527 million adjustment is large enough to move bear value from above the $41.18 market price to below it, so the classification can change a valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a daily or monthly minimum-cash analysis across the seasonal cycle, reconcile restricted and foreign cash plus near-term payments and revolver usage, and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Supplier finance may be an unrecognized debt-like claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $370.4 million at June 30, 2026, or $3.45 per diluted share; down $68.1 million from $438.5 million at December 31, 2025; deducting the June balance would reduce computed bear value from $43.21 to $39.76 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If supplier finance represents incremental financing and its working-capital benefit was excluded from OE, failing to deduct or otherwise fund the claim overstates the equity bridge and sustainable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Suppliers’ receivables included in this SCF program were $ 438.5 million and $ 303.7 million at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and were included in accounts payable in our Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and its latest balance are demonstrated, but debt-like classification and any double count are unresolved. It remains in accounts payable, can run for up to 210 days, and declined during the 2026 seasonal build. If it is ordinary recurring trade credit, a separate deduction may be inappropriate; if it extended payment terms and OE excludes working-capital investment, the omitted claim is large enough to change the bear conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 SCF invoices to ordinary supplier terms and historical payable days, identify the incremental working-capital financing benefit captured by OE, and rerun either with normalized working capital or a debt-like bridge deduction, but not both.

audit_findings.title: Multiemployer withdrawal payments may exceed the cost retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.0 million total future cash expenditures, or $0.34 per diluted share before discounting; approximately $1.8 million annual cash-expense shortfall, equal to 0.5% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Accounting earnings retain approximately $0.8 million of annual accretion while owner cash outflow is approximately $2.6 million, potentially overstating annual OE by about $1.8 million unless separately reflected.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our total future expected cash expenditures related to this withdrawal were $ 36.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-versus-expense mismatch is demonstrated, but its scale is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion. Even the undiscounted $36.0 million total is only about 0.7% of the $5,408 million base equity value and $0.34 per share; the recurring incremental shortfall is about 0.5% of anchor OE. A correction is appropriate for precision but not materiality.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether OE already deducts the $2.6 million cash payment or whether the liability is separately reflected; if not, replace accretion with cash payments while avoiding double counting.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may capitalize acquisition-funded growth for free
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; modeled 3% growth adds $775 million of equity value and $7.23 per share over the 0% case, while 5% growth adds $1,365 million and $12.73 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The growth rates increase forecast OE and terminal value, while an absent acquisition perimeter can omit purchase consideration, integration investment and incremental interest required to produce that growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Our future growth will depend in large part on additional acquisitions of consumer goods packaging businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: No specific future acquisition spending requirement is established, so the omission is not a demonstrated dollar error. It is nevertheless material because the valuation perimeter is null, Silgan states that future growth depends in large part on acquisitions, and the modeled growth premium is large enough to affect the conclusion. Organic growth may support some growth, but the current record does not establish that 3%–5% can be achieved without acquisition capital.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic and acquired growth using historical volume, pricing, margin and acquisition contributions; demonstrate organically funded growth after maintenance and productivity spending or rerun each scenario with the acquisition outlays and after-tax interest needed to achieve it.
